alt: Parsons’s instrumental breadwinner role for husbands and expressive caring role for wives, then the triple shift of paid work, domestic labour and emotion work carried by many employed women.
caption: Women’s expressive role becomes a triple shift once they also take paid work.

alt: Five reasons roles change: women’s employment, feminist ideas and equality laws, decline of manual industry, smaller families and technology, and changing fatherhood. These lead to Young and Willmott’s symmetrical family or Gershuny’s lagged adaptation.
caption: Roles are changing, but how far and how fast is disputed.

alt: A grid applying three distinctions, tasks versus responsibility, routine versus occasional work and paid help, to men’s and women’s domestic work, with Edgell and Pahl on power and money.
caption: Counting tasks hides who carries responsibility and power.

alt: Three explanations of family violence: Dobash and Dobash on patriarchal authority, radical feminists on control, and others on poverty, stress and alcohol. A note covers under-reporting and changing ideas of discipline.
caption: Feminists see control where others see stress, and much violence goes unrecorded.

alt: A timeline from medieval Europe, where children joined the adult world early, through the growth of a separate childhood and child labour and education laws, to Postman’s claim that television blurs the boundary. Cards contrast children in rural Bolivia with wealthy societies.
caption: Childhood differs over time and between societies.

alt: Smaller families, lower infant mortality, rising living standards and expert parenting advice lead to the child-centred family. Gittins’s idea of age patriarchy and class variation qualify it.
caption: Child centredness grew, but adults still hold power over children.

alt: Reasons adult children return home to form boomerang families and the mixed effects, then a comparison of older people’s status where filial obligation is strong or status is tied to paid work, and grandparent roles.
caption: Generational roles stretch as children return and lives lengthen.
